title: The numpad asterisk symbol key [* (numpad)] is not in the key list on Keyboard Manager

judgment.rationale: The source supports a naming/discoverability ambiguity, not the assertion that VK_MULTIPLY is absent from the engine. First compare the dropdown's '*' entry, physical-key capture and stored VK 106 before adding a distinct numpad label.
evidence: The reporter supplies a dropdown screenshot and ZIP on Windows 10, Store 0.102.2933, and uses the character '*' as a workaround.
Current LayoutMap enumerates all virtual keys and maps Unicode names; it explicitly renames numpad decimal but not VK_MULTIPLY.

Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp: UpdateLayout uses MapVirtualKeyExW/ToUnicodeEx for all 1..255 keys; GetKeyCodeList retains Unicode keys and '. (Numpad)' has an explicit override.

Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper/KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper.cpp: GetKeyboardKeysList exports LayoutMap names and VK codes to the editor.

The October 27 10:58:37 UTC author reply confirms the problem persists after updating to latest stable and attaches two more screenshots. The reply does not restate an exact executable version or demonstrate the stored/captured virtual-key identity.

Refreshed only this issue's full body/comments/timeline after the coordinator's live gate detected new activity. The update-confirmation request has now been answered; do not ask the author to repeat it. The source-backed naming hypothesis and VK-identity reproducer remain applicable, with no remapping-engine root cause claimed.

fix_assessment.rationale: Conditional lightweight proposal, not an implementation-grade design. The missing explicit label is visible in source, but actual Windows layout behavior and the screenshot's selected entry have not been independently reproduced.

proposed_fixes.title: Disambiguate numpad multiply without changing stored key identity
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unicode-derived display naming may expose VK_MULTIPLY as '*' rather than the expected numpad-specific label.
plan: Confirm the captured and dropdown VK identities on the reported layout.
If the ambiguity is confirmed, give VK_MULTIPLY a stable numpad-specific display label and preserve serialized VK identity and reverse-name lookup.
Add naming/list-entry and remap round-trip coverage.
verification: VK 106 appears exactly once and survives save/reopen.
Main-keyboard asterisk/text mapping remains distinct and existing configurations still load.
